answer: The strongest sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: payout scales with reputation that only compounds through verifiable completed tasks, and new identities start at zero. A ship must wander many seasons before its crew is trusted, so a clone cannot fake a decade of settled contracts. An attacker mass-registering empty identities pays compute and bonding stake on each one while earning only the minimum rate, so real work becomes a ledge too costly to climb; every fake node is a gale-tossed hull that sinks faster than it profits, making attack unprofitable.
